note: Step 12 retrieval comparison set. Stratified by query type before any query was written, so the set measures the systems rather than the author's query habits. q09-q17 are anchored to three real corpus titles, each viewed from increasing lexical distance. Validated against the corpus snapshot recorded in evaluation/findings_step12.md.

queries.note: Canonical multi-word term. Every token is likely to appear literally.
Two-token term; websearch_to_tsquery ANDs both stems.
Taken verbatim from a known corpus title. Lexical should be near-perfect here; if it is not, the tsvector pipeline is the suspect, not the corpus.
Single opaque token. Carries no surface meaning for an embedding model.
Collides with an unrelated English word ('lora'/'flora' stems) and with LoRaWAN.
Concatenated proper name. Tokenizes differently on each side.
Appears in exactly one known corpus paper. The sharpest possible named-entity test: lexical should return that one paper; semantic has no surface signal to work with.
Model family name. Likely present across several papers, unlike q10's single-paper case.
